study_identification_part.si4_title: Deep Normative Tractometry for Identifying Joint White Matter Macro- and Micro-structural Abnormalities in Alzheimer's Disease

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose and evaluate a Deep Normative Tractometry (DNT) framework based on a variational autoencoder trained on healthy controls to learn the normative distribution of along-tract macro- and micro-structural profiles, and assess generalizability via transfer learning to detect abnormalities in MCI and Alzheimer's disease.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of AD/MCI versus controls using along-tract tests; visualization with p-values (−log10 p) and Cohen's d; comparison against BUAN tractometry.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: DNT detected widespread diffusivity abnormalities along tracts in MCI/AD that aligned closely with BUAN; incorporating tract geometry enables distinguishing anisotropy from macrostructural changes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across multiple bundles, DNT revealed significant along-tract differences in MD and FA for AD and MCI and additional abnormalities in tract shape; heatmaps show many significant segments with patterns comparable to BUAN, and tract renderings illustrate spatial localization of deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Model pre-trained on a large control dataset and transferred to an Indian cohort; outputs include along-tract abnormality maps for FA, MD, and shape, with qualitative and quantitative comparisons to BUAN.
